description.value: The study examined whether abstinence-induced changes in striatal responses to monetary and smoking rewards predicted lapse during a contingency-managed smoking quit attempt.

spans.text: The present study examined associations between abstinence-induced changes in striatal reward processing and the ability to maintain abstinence during a quit attempt supported by contingency management.

Non-abstinent activation to smoking and monetary rewards was entered first, followed by activation to each reward type during abstinence; age and sex were included as covariates. Significance was set at p < 0.025 to control for comparisons across the two hemisphere models.

spans.text: For each model, activation to smoking and monetary rewards during non-abstinence were entered during a first step to examine baseline differences between lapsers and abstainers in a satiated state. instructions.value: Participants guessed whether a computer-generated number would be higher or lower than 5 by pressing a button. They could earn monetary reward or puffs of a cigarette if their guess was correct; rewards were delivered after the scan during a one-hour waiting period, during which they were required to abstain from smoking other than earned puffs.

stimuli.value: A question mark, a button-choice guessing display, and pictures representing the possible reward: a stack of dollar bills for $0.50, a cigarette for a puff, or a blue notebook for no reward. The actual number and win or no-win feedback were then presented.
